title: Word and Writing: log and graph
short: log means word, reason or study; graph and gram mean write or draw.
trouble: -logy means "the study of" in most science words (biology), but log alone often means word or speech (eulogy, dialogue).

blocks.html: Two Greek roots fill the pages of every school. log (also logy) means “word,” “reason” or “study”: biology is the study of life, logic is reasoning and a dialogue is words between people. graph (also gram) means “write” or “draw”: an autograph is written by yourself, a biography is a written life and a telegram is writing sent from far away.

blocks.html: At the end of a word, -logy usually means “the study of”: biology (life), geology (the earth), anthropology (human beings). Elsewhere, log usually means word or speech: a eulogy is good words, a monologue is one person’s speech, and an analogy compares one thing to another by reasoning.

head: Word and meaning
Parts, and what they say
rows:
eulogy
a speech of praise, especially for someone who has died

analogy
a comparison that explains one thing by its likeness to another

ana- according to + log reason + -y
→ “according to reason (a matching proportion)”

anthropology
the study of human beings and their cultures

anthrop human being + -logy study of
→ “the study of human beings”

biography
the story of a person’s life written by someone else

telegram
a message sent by wire and printed

blocks.title: Build a word
blocks.q: A biography is a life story written by someone else. What do you call a life story a person writes about himself or herself?

blocks.name: vo-word

entry.def: a speech or writing in praise of someone, especially someone who has died
entry.ex: Grandpa’s oldest friend gave a warm {eulogy}, full of funny stories, at his memorial.
entry.ctx: Rather than list the scientist’s awards, the {eulogy} described her kindness: the students she fed, the letters she answered and the neighbors she helped.
entry.note: A eulogy (praise) is not an elegy (a sad poem or song).

mn.cue: EU-LOGY: GOOD WORDS about a life
mn.text: At the memorial, Maya steps to the podium and shares warm, funny stories about her grandfather’s life; her speech of praise is a {eulogy}.

scene.alt: A teen at a podium shares kind memories of her grandfather beside flowers and a framed picture.

blocks.cap: A word from the list: eulogy.

blocks.name: vo-word

entry.def: a comparison that explains one thing by its likeness to another
entry.ex: The coach used an {analogy}: a team is like a clock, and every little gear matters.
entry.ctx: To explain how the computer’s memory works, the author drew an {analogy} to a library, with files as books and the processor as a busy librarian.
entry.etym: From Greek analogia, “proportion”: ana (according to) + logos (ratio, reason).

mn.text: To explain how the brain stores memories, Professor Edwin points from his head to his laptop: “It works like this!” That comparison is an {analogy}.

cast.say: The brain is LIKE a computer!

scene.alt: A professor compares the brain to the laptop on his desk while a student listens.

blocks.html: Reading every log as “study of.” -logy at the end of a word usually means the study of (biology), but log elsewhere often means word or speech: a eulogy is not “the study of good”; it is a speech of praise.
